title: Club-neutral images of the four CourtHive components
description: Build versioned, club-neutral images of the tournament server, the identity service (courthive-hiveid), TMX and the public pages from the latest upstream. Each fork carries a jdt-bundle branch (upstream commit, link overrides removed, the smallest source changes, build files); the identity service is built from the exact upstream commit with no fork (deploy/images/courthive-hiveid). CI drafts in each fork build on push and publish to GitHub Container Registry on a bundle-v tag.

recommended_model.name: Opus 5.5
recommended_model.rationale: Build and configuration changes across three TypeScript projects with known past pitfalls.

acceptance_criteria: Four images build locally under their final names and tags (courthive-server 4.19.1-jdt.1, courthive-hiveid 0.5.0-jdt.1, courthive-tmx 8.61.0-jdt.1, courthive-public 1.23.7-jdt.1), each usable under any hostname without rebuilding
No built file contains jim.tennis, the author's server address or any secret; the front ends contact no host but their own on load
Tags carry the upstream version; labels carry the upstream commit and fork commit
Each image carries the upstream MIT text, a NOTICE and third-party licences under /licenses
The build fails clearly if a link: override is present
The server image contains src/scripts/admin-user.mjs; front-end images contain no source maps
What the front ends can still contact after a person's choice (Google Fonts, map tiles, linked sheets, typed-in image addresses) is listed in docs/outbound_connections.md
Nothing is pushed to GitHub or a registry until the owner says so; then each fork's CI builds and publishes on tag after its checks pass

files_to_create: CI workflows and Dockerfiles in each fork
notes: See docs/courthive_bundle_design.md (rewritten 2026-11-22 for latest upstream), sections 1 and 2.
Fork branches: jdt-bundle in competition-factory-server, TMX and courthive-public (local, unpushed). BUNDLE.md in each lists the changes and how to move to a newer upstream.
Node 26 images have no corepack: the Dockerfiles install the pnpm named in packageManager.
Pushing workflow files needs the workflow token scope.

testing_requirements: Run all three images locally under two hostnames and complete a sign-in and a tournament page load on each

context.user_story: As a club, I want the tournament software as ready-made images so that I never build it.
context.programme: Club-readiness programme (sprints 019-024). Agreed constraints: BHPLTA clubs only; each club self-hosts its own instance; the original author must have no access to any other club's instance (no seeded accounts, no shared or default secrets, no phone-home); passkeys are the default sign-in with passwords as an optional fallback; the captain role is real; SQLite is the only supported database; CourtHive is bundled as an opt-in part of the package so clubs can run their own club championships.

status_note: Completed 2026-11-23. The forks' jdt-bundle branches are pushed and the four images are published as public packages on ghcr.io (amd64 only, pushed from the maintainer's machine; anonymous pull checked). The fork CI workflows and bundle-smoke.yml have never run because GitHub Actions is billing-locked for this account.
